Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant transition you're going through as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common experiences for many new mothers. It's essential to remember that this assessment is not about judging your feelings or experiences but rather about creating a safe and supportive space for us to explore them together.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm here to listen without any judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand how you've been feeling over the past week. These questions are designed to be straightforward and will allow us to have a more in-depth conversation about your emotional state. I'll ask each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you're comfortable. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'm here to support you throughout this process.

Let's begin with the first question, which is about how you've been feeling in general. Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. I think so. I mean, I still enjoy some things, like watching my baby smile or play, but it's not as easy for me to laugh like it used to be. Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think, "Oh, this is supposed to be fun," but it doesn't always feel that way. But, at the same time, I do have moments where I can laugh and feel happy, like when my husband makes a joke or something. It's just... it's not as frequent as it used to be, I guess. And sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy, like I'm putting on a show for everyone else, but deep down, I'm just feeling really tired and overwhelmed. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I think I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, but not as much as I used to. Some days are better than others, and when my baby smiles or does something cute, it always makes me laugh. But on the days when I'm feeling really tired or stressed, it's harder for me to find the humor in things. Like, the other day, my husband was trying to make me laugh, and I just couldn't. I felt so overwhelmed and anxious about the baby's health that I just couldn't shake off the feeling, no matter how hard he tried to make me smile. But, overall, I'd say I can still laugh and see the funny side of things, just not as easily or as often as I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, I haven't been looking forward to things as much as I used to. I mean, I'll plan something, like a walk with my baby or a visit with friends, and I'll think, "Oh, this will be nice," but when the time comes, I don't always feel as excited or enthusiastic as I thought I would. Sometimes I even feel a little anxious about leaving the house or meeting new people with my baby. It's like, I know I should be enjoying these moments, but it's just been harder for me to feel that way lately. But, there are some things that I still look forward to, like my daily coffee or a warm bath after a long day. Those little things can be really comforting and give me something to look forward to. It's just... it's not the same as it used to be, you know? I feel like I've lost a little bit of my sparkle, and it's hard to get excited about things when I'm feeling so tired and overwhelmed all the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I'd say that's happened to me a few times. Like, if my baby is crying and I don't know how to calm her down, I'll start thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I do this?" or "I'm a terrible mother for not being able to soothe my own baby." It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's hard not to blame myself when things don't go as planned. And sometimes, it's the little things, like if I forget to pack something for the baby or if I don't make a perfect meal, and I'll think, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I get my act together?" But, I try to remind myself that everyone makes mistakes, and it's okay not to be perfect. It's just... sometimes it's hard to shake off that feeling of inadequacy, you know? But, it's not all the time, and I'm trying to be kinder to myself and remind myself that I'm doing the best I can.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... I'd say that's happened to me a bit. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something, like, "What if she's not gaining enough weight?" or "What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate her development?" And it's not like there's any real reason for me to be worried, it's just... my mind starts racing and I get caught up in these worst-case scenarios. But, usually, I can calm myself down and think, "Okay, everything is fine, I'm just being paranoid." It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's hard not to worry when you're responsible for this tiny human being. Sometimes, I'll even find myself worrying about things that are totally out of my control, like, "What if she gets sick?" or "What if something happens to her when I'm not around?" But, like I said, I can usually talk myself down and remind myself that I'm doing everything I can to take care of her. It's just... sometimes those anxious thoughts can be really overwhelming.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah... I think I've felt that way a few times. Like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic or anxiety wash over me, and I'm not even sure why. It's not like anything specific is happening, it's just... my heart starts racing, and I feel like I'm going to cry or something. But, it's not all the time, and it's usually not too intense. I mean, I can still function and take care of my baby, it's just... it's like this underlying feeling of unease that I haven't been able to shake. Sometimes, I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll just feel overwhelmed, like I'm in way over my head. But, I've been trying to take some deep breaths and remind myself that everything is okay, and that I'm doing the best I can. It's just... it's hard to explain, it's like this feeling of being on edge, all the time. But, like I said, it's not constant, and I'm trying to manage it.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely been true for me lately. I mean, taking care of a new baby is overwhelming, and some days it feels like everything is just piling up on me. I'll be trying to manage the baby's schedule, and the housework, and cooking, and everything else, and it just feels like too much. I'll be sitting there, feeling exhausted, and thinking, "How am I going to get everything done?" And sometimes, it feels like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. But, I've been trying to prioritize, and focus on one thing at a time, and that's helped a bit. And my husband has been really supportive, too, so that's been a big help. But, yeah, some days it definitely feels like things are getting on top of me, and I just want to crawl back into bed and hide. Especially when I'm feeling tired, which is most of the time, it feels like. But, I'm trying to stay on top of things, and not let it all get too overwhelming.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Sleeping... yeah, that's been a challenge for me. But, it's not always because I'm unhappy, it's just... my mind is always racing, and I have trouble winding down at night. Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed, and I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do the next day, or worrying about the baby, and it's hard to turn my brain off. But, it's not like I'm lying awake all night, every night, feeling miserable or anything. It's just... some nights are harder than others. And, to be honest, most of the time, I'm just so exhausted that I can fall asleep pretty easily. But, there are some nights where I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll have trouble falling back asleep, and that's usually when my mind starts to wander, and I'll start thinking about all the things that are stressing me out. But, overall, I'd say I sleep okay, considering I'm a new mom and all. I mean, I'm not getting as much sleep as I used to, but that's just part of the deal, right.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah... I'd say that's happened to me a few times. I mean, being a new mom can be really overwhelming, and some days it feels like everything is just too much. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's not always because of anything specific, it's just... I'll be feeling tired, and stressed, and anxious, and it all just feels really overwhelming. And sometimes, I'll just start crying, and I won't even know why. It's like, my emotions are just really close to the surface, and it doesn't take much to set me off. But, it's not like I'm feeling sad or miserable all the time. I mean, I have good days and bad days, like anyone, I guess. And, most of the time, I can shake off the sad feelings and focus on the positive things, like my baby's smile, or the fact that I'm lucky to have such a supportive husband. But, yeah, sometimes it's hard to escape those feelings of sadness, and it feels like they're just lurking beneath the surface, waiting to pounce.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah... I'd say that's happened to me a few times. I mean, like I said, being a new mom can be really overwhelming, and some days it feels like everything is just too much. And, yeah, I've cried a few times when I've just felt really overwhelmed and sad. It's not always because of anything specific, it's just... I'll be feeling tired, and stressed, and anxious, and it all just feels really too much to handle. And, sometimes, I'll just start crying, and I won't even know why. It's like, my emotions are just really close to the surface, and it doesn't take much to set me off. But, it's not like I'm crying all the time or anything. I mean, it's just been a few times, and it's usually when I'm feeling really exhausted and overwhelmed. Like, the other day, I was trying to get the baby to sleep, and she just wouldn't settle down, and I was feeling so frustrated and tired, and I just started crying. But, my husband was there, and he helped me calm down, and we figured out a way to get the baby to sleep, and I felt better after that. So, yeah, I've cried a few times, but it's not like it's a constant thing or anything.

4. Provide patient with resources for <med>postpartum depression</med> support, such as support groups and online resources
5. Encourage patient to reach out to family and friends for emotional support
